body_text:
The additive monoid $\mathbb{N}$ embeds into the additive group
$\mathbb{Z}$ by $n\mapsto[n,0]$. More generally, every monoid
homomorphism from $\mathbb{N}$ into an abelian group extends
uniquely to a group homomorphism from $\mathbb{Z}$. This universal
property characterizes the integers as the group completion of the
natural numbers.
